newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up sharply in winter on one active trade.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up sharply in winter on one active trade.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices went sharply up next winter and in the gas year from October, with one player seen behind most of the deals done on Thursday, traders and brokers said.

A single player reported doing 14 of the trades on the cash market, although a trader denied that they had just been buyers. "We're trading, both buying and selling. It's a misinterpretation by the market that we're only buying," he said.

"The fact that the market is running up is because of the fact that net out there there are more buyers than sellers," he added "This is by no means an outrageous price that we've run up to here," he said.
But another trader was sceptical about the level of trading, saying simply "it's up on the back of one party actively buying."

Many players were comparatively inactive. One reported that most of its efforts were concentrated on preparing bids for the Transco storage tender, details of which were released over last weekend. The deadline for bids is 1500 GMT on Friday, and one dealer said he was delaying submitting a bid until the last possible moment, and taking account of recent price movements before doing so.

Nearly all the activity done on Thursday was in Q4 97, the gas year starting in October, and Q1 98. Outside these periods, a single deal was reported in Q2 98 at 11.225 pence a therm, with some volumes done for the day ahead at 9.30 pence a therm.
Q4 traded as high as 12.90 pence, the gas year up to 12.90 pence, and Q1 98 at up to 16.60 pence. But a broker said that offers were even higher by the close, as the market continued to move up.

The IPE futures market followed physical prices up. A total of 225 lots were traded, the highest number for nearly a month. Every month with the exception of March 98 settled higher, and the winter saw the steepest rises on futures, in line with direction on the physical market.
